walkthroughs.body_html:
Foundations of Physics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Foundations of Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Foundations of Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A proton consists of which quarks?
options: udd
uud
uds
uuu

mcqs.q: In β⁻ decay, the exchange particle is:
options: Photon
W⁻ boson
Gluon
Z boson

mcqs.q: Does light always travel at the same speed?
options: Yes — c is a universal constant in every situation.
Only in a vacuum; in any material medium (water, glass) light travels more slowly, which is what causes refraction.
Light must go from a less dense to a denser medium.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.

mcqs.q: What condition must be met for total internal reflection to occur?
options: Light must go from a less dense to a denser medium.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
Light must travel from a denser to a less dense medium AND strike the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle.
Any angle is fine as long as the light is going into a less dense medium.

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: Light must go from a less dense to a denser medium.
The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quark”?
options: In particle interactions, charge, baryon number, lepton number and energy/momentum are conserved.
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).
A fundamental particle (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) that makes up hadrons.
A neutron decays to a proton, electron and antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Exchange particle”?
options: A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
A fundamental particle (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) that makes up hadrons.
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).

A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
